segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for jumping on, Karen. I wanted to clean up the open items before your September 3 go-live: 38 seats, the advanced reporting add-on, and the services block at $6,800. Is that still the right scope?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. The issue is the SSO setup. Your implementation coordinator told my IT lead yesterday they had no record that SSO needed to be ready before go-live. We agreed on the July 22 call that SSO was required by August 27, and I repeated that in email. So now my team is hearing it is a two-week turnaround, which doesn't work.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: You're right. I found the note in our thread, and I agreed to that date with you. I did not get it into the implementation notes, so the implementation team was surprised and treated SSO like a later phase item. That's on me. I already asked them to pull in the engineer, but yeah, that should not have landed on your IT lead as new information.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, but practically, can it still be done? We have training scheduled for August 29 and September 1, and people cannot use another password for two days and then switch.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I hear you. The engineer can start tomorrow morning if your IdP metadata is over by 3 p.m. today. They'll target a test connection by August 25 and production cutover August 27. I'll send that in writing after this call.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Fine. The other thing is the invoice. Accounting received an invoice for $9,450 due August 15, but the agreement was net 45 and split across two invoices, one in August and one in October. That was a condition for signature.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, and I need to apologize there too. We agreed to split billing and net 45 in the final redline, but I didn't pass that instruction to the billing team when the order was booked. They generated the standard single invoice on net 30, so they were just following what they had. I should have made sure billing had the exception before anything went out.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That caused some noise here, because procurement thought you were changing terms after signature. Please get the corrected invoice to ap@northlakeparts.com and copy me.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Absolutely. Deal desk approved the exception this morning, and billing is voiding the $9,450 invoice. You'll get invoice one for $4,725 with a due date of September 29, and invoice two for $4,725 dated October 1, due November 15.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Send the SSO timeline, the corrected billing details, and the seat list template. If those three things are right, we're good to keep the September 3 go-live.
